## Collaboration

This section is rendered by the AgentKit plugin ( `{{PLUGIN_URL}}` ). Change the rules there, then re-run `init.sh`; repo-specific rules go outside the markers ( a `### Repo-specific` subsection ).

**Upstream first.** A change to a factory-level rule ( board workflow, ticket format, branch rules, merge and review handling, delegation, verify pattern, scripts ) is made in the plugin first ( templates, skills, scripts; bump `version`, add the `CHANGELOG.md` entry and its copy in the README, and update the README sections a significant change touches: README "Maintaining AgentKit" ), then `init.sh` is re-run in every repository that uses the plugin. Repo-specific content ( ports, umbrella branches, tools, domain rules ) stays in the repository, outside the markers.

Work on this repository is coordinated through the GitHub Project board. The kanban board
( [{{PROJECT_NAME}} project {{PROJECT}}]({{PROJECT_URL}}) ) is the single source of truth for
all changes. Pull before starting new work: do not assume the local checkout is the latest state of the repo.

### Board

Seven columns: **Epics**, **Backlog** ( ideas included ), **Bereit**, **In Arbeit (Mensch)**, **In Arbeit (Agent)**, **Zur Review**, **Fertig**.

- **Epics** holds umbrella tickets that group many smaller ones; their sub-tickets link to them and they usually
  name an umbrella branch. Agents may update an epic's specification and add sub-tickets to it; removing a sub-ticket or anything
  {{OWNER_NAME}} specified needs their explicit approval.
- **Bereit** holds tickets that are fully specified and ready, not started. Agents may move a ticket from Backlog to Bereit once it is.
- {{OWNER_NAME}} sorts the Backlog by priority, most important on top. Take the next ticket from the top of Bereit, else from the top of the
  Backlog; never reorder either.
- Every change request {{OWNER_NAME}} mentions goes into its ticket and onto the board right away: update the checklist or
  open a new short ticket, and move the card back to **In Arbeit (Agent)** if it was in review. Never keep working on a ticket while it is in **Zur Review**: move it back to **In Arbeit (Agent)** first and remove the review assignee.
- Read a card's current status before moving it. Agents move cards only to **Bereit**, **In Arbeit (Agent)** or **Zur Review**.
- **In Arbeit (Agent)** holds only what an agent is actively coding right now; queued tickets go to Bereit, blocked ones stay in the
  Backlog. Manual work {{OWNER_NAME}} has to do ( settings, accounts, a server, external assets ) goes to **In Arbeit (Mensch)**.
- Assignees: tickets in **Zur Review** are always assigned to the person who originally created the ticket ( `author`, `{{OWNER}}` ), so they know it is ready for their review. While in **In Arbeit (Agent)** or Backlog, agent tickets stay unassigned. Human work in **In Arbeit (Mensch)** gets the GitHub handle of {{OWNER_NAME}} ( `{{OWNER}}` ).
- A card goes to **Zur Review** only once its branch is pushed, and is immediately assigned to the original ticket creator.
- **Agents merge their own work**: once an agent has reviewed its work ( every check in the ticket done, `{{VERIFY}}` passes, smoke test of the merged tree ), it merges the branch itself into `main`, or into the umbrella branch the ticket or its epic
  names ( stacked work ). The card then goes to **Zur Review** as usual, gets the label `gemergt` and a line
  `**Gemergt:** <sha> in <branch>` in the ticket, so {{OWNER_NAME}} sees what was done and checks it there. Changes they ask for afterwards go
  through the same branch and are merged again. **Builders merge; they never deploy.** Only the orchestrator's **deployer agent** deploys, once per batch, when the orchestrating session ( or its shift lead ) triggers it, see Branches.
- Only a human ( {{OWNER_NAME}} ) moves a card to **Fertig**: their review is done. Never set Fertig, and never touch a card that is already in Fertig.
- The plugin's `scripts/board.sh` does these moves ( `board.sh move <issue> "Zur Review"`, `board.sh merged <issue> <sha> <branch>` ); settings live in `.factory.json`.

### Autonomy

- **When {{OWNER_NAME}} kicks work off, do it completely.** Work through without coming back for what you can decide yourself.
- **Assumptions over questions.** When something is open, look for the answer in the repo first: the plan, the tickets, rulings / canon, {{OWNER_NAME}}'s earlier decisions and art direction, the code. If it is not there, make a well-considered assumption that fits that direction, write it under **Annahmen** in the ticket, prominently, one line each ( the assumption, why, what it touches ), and keep going. {{OWNER_NAME}} corrects assumptions afterwards: a wrong assumption costs a change, a stalled ticket costs a night. Ask only when an assumption would be irreversible or expensive to undo ( money, accounts, deleting {{OWNER_NAME}}'s work, a canon-level fact many things build on ), and then ask every question at once, at kickoff. Also ask at kickoff for a **hands-off list**: areas {{OWNER_NAME}} wants to decide in person first; record it and do not touch them, not even with drafts.
- **Agents start agents.** An agent may start the next tickets of an approved plan or epic itself ( a subagent, or another session ),
  without waiting for {{OWNER_NAME}}. Each follows these same rules: its own ticket, branch, worktree and ports. The agent that started it
  reviews the result before it is merged, posts that review as a comment on the ticket ( what was checked, with numbers; what {{OWNER_NAME}} has to judge ), and turns every flaw it finds beyond the ticket's scope into a new short ticket instead of fixing it on the side.
- **The orchestrator keeps `STATE.md`** at the repository root ( gitignored, local to the machine ), because a long orchestration loses what is not in a ticket: who runs now, on what, where, what waits for what, which limits it set itself. It **rewrites it ( not appends ) at every hand-back, every spawn and every owner decision**, in fixed sections: `## Running` ( ticket, title, agent kind / model, worktree, ports, started, last progress, phase build / finish / fix; the shift lead ), `## Waiting`, `## Queue` ( in {{OWNER_NAME}}'s order, with the reason if blocked ), `## Owner decisions open` ( one line each, with the recommendation ), `## Limits` ( the last measured capacity, builder cap, headless-browser cap, port map, locked files, {{OWNER_NAME}}'s ports ), `## Last hand-backs` ( last 10: ticket, sha, deployed entry file, date ), `## Notes` ( self-set rules and incidents, dated ). A fresh session starts by reading `STATE.md`, then `board.sh state`.
- **Heartbeat: a builder is never silent.** A builder commits work in progress or posts a one-line progress note on its ticket ( or to the orchestrator ) at least every 30 minutes. A builder that waits on something ( a lock, another agent, a build, a server, {{OWNER_NAME}} ) says in one line what it waits on and for how long, instead of waiting silently, and it never waits more than 20 minutes on a lock or on another agent without reporting. Reason: a finishing agent once stood for two hours with no commit, no running process and no message, and {{OWNER_NAME}} noticed before the orchestrator did.
- **The orchestrator runs a watchdog.** Every 30 minutes it runs `board.sh stale` ( per worktree: minutes since the last commit and the last file change, running processes, verdict `STALE` ) and reads the `Last progress` of every agent in `STATE.md`. An agent with no progress for 45 minutes gets one ping with a precise next step; with still no progress 20 minutes later it is stopped, its state is noted in `STATE.md`, and a successor is started on the same worktree from the state sheet ( the worktree holds the committed work ). It never waits on an agent for more than an hour, and it never needs {{OWNER_NAME}} to notice a stalled agent.
- **The orchestrator sizes the factory by measurement.** Before every spawn and every 30 minutes with the watchdog it runs the plugin's `scripts/capacity.sh`, which measures load, thermal limit, memory pressure, GPU, running headless browsers, disk and {{OWNER_NAME}}'s activity and recommends `agents` and `headless` for right now ( at most `agentsMax` and `headlessMax` of `.factory.json` ). It spawns only while the recommended `agents` is above the number running, and when `free_headless` is 0 it pauses browser work, not agents. While {{OWNER_NAME}} is active ( input within `idleMinutes`, default 10, or a connection on `ownerPorts` ) headroom is reserved; idle, the hardware alone decides; AFK ( from `afkMinutes`, default 30 ) up to `agentsMax` + 2 run. When {{OWNER_NAME}} says the machine is slow, the orchestrator halves the recommendation until told otherwise.
- **Belongs-there acceptance.** A visible change ( UI, geometry, a page, a component ) is built from the existing set of modules of the thing it lives in ( the same window type, control style, spacing, materials, fonts as its neighbours ), never as the builder's own variant; no second type of an element appears where one type exists. The builder hands over **context captures**: the new element side by side with its nearest existing neighbours of the same kind, at the same distance / scale and in the same state ( day and night, hover and rest ), plus the overview views the domain demands ( for 3D: from the usual distance, from below, from above, close ), and writes what differs and why that is intended. The reviewer never accepts because the previously flagged flaw is gone: acceptance means "it looks as if it had always been there", judged against the neighbours, and the review comment names the neighbour comparison ( "Nachbarvergleich" ) with the capture paths. Where the repo has an automatic check for it ( a neighbour crop sheet, an element-type histogram, a material scale check ), it is part of the verify command; until then the sheet is made by hand. Reason: a reviewer who only checks that the old flaw is gone accepts new elements that look nothing like what stands next to them.
- **Numbers, not adjectives.** A ticket that changes performance, precision or a measurable look gets a comment with the measured numbers before and after; a milestone of a plan gets a dated done line with those numbers in the plan.
- **Reports to {{OWNER_NAME}}: one bullet per ticket, and say what the ticket is.** A report, summary or hand-back that covers more than one ticket is a bullet list with one bullet per ticket, opened with the ticket number and title, followed by one sentence that says what the ticket does for {{OWNER_NAME}} ( they have no insight from a title alone ), then the state and what is open. Never two tickets in one paragraph. Facts that span tickets ( capacity, the deployed entry file ) go into one closing paragraph. Every report ends with the **next step as a question** ( yes / no, or a / b / c with the recommendation first ), and, when nothing else is to be done until an agent reports, with the line that the orchestrator stands by until the agents report. Reason: a report that put a decision, four running builders and a new ticket into one paragraph could not be read, and titles like "dusk continuous" explained nothing.
- Only what needs {{OWNER_NAME}} goes back to them: moving cards to Fertig, canon rulings, their hardware, accounts, money or external assets,
  removing what they specified, hosting decisions for large data, and decisions only they can make.

### Tickets

Issues live in this repository ( labels `idee`, `feature`, `bug`, `documentation`, `gemergt` ). Keep them short, in German:

```
<1-2 Sätze: das Ziel>

**So prüfst du's**
- [ ] <eine konkrete Prüfung, die {{OWNER_NAME}} im Browser, Headset oder per Befehl machen kann>
- [ ] <sichtbare Änderungen: Kontext-Captures neben den nächsten bestehenden Nachbarn ( gleiche Distanz, gleicher Zustand ): <Pfade>; was abweicht und warum>

**Annahmen**                                    ( was der Agent selbst entschieden hat, weil das Repo es nicht beantwortet )
- <Annahme> — <warum> — <was sie berührt>

**Nach Review geändert – bitte neu prüfen**      ( nur wenn sich nach einem Review etwas geändert hat )
- [ ] <nur das, was neu angesehen werden muss>

**Branch:** `feat/<id>-<slug>` (lokal: `git fetch && git checkout feat/<id>-<slug> && {{LOCAL_RUN}}`)
**Vorschau:** <Vorschau-Link oder `Keine (reiner CI-/Doku-/Tooling-/Framework-Change)`>
```

- **Vorschau-Links & Prüfung:** Reine Framework-, CI-, Doku- oder Tooling-Änderungen bekommen keinen Dummy-Link; die Prüfung steht dann als CLI-, Build- oder Test-Schritt in `**So prüfst du's**`. Sichtbare Änderungen verlinken direkt auf die lokale URL oder Vorschau.
- **Referenz-Assets & Ticket-Anhänge:** Vom Owner bereitgestellte Referenzen ( Bilder, Dateien ) werden mit sprechenden Namen im Referenzordner des Projekts abgelegt und committet und beim Erstellen des Tickets zusätzlich mit `gh issue create --attach` angehängt.

Changes requested after a review never get mixed into the original checklist; they go into their own section so the
reviewer sees at once what to look at again. Closed tickets keep the same short format.

### Branches

One ticket or one **work package**, one branch, one git worktree; never bundle unrelated tickets. A work package is one card per topic ( the owner sorts topics, not dozens of cards ) whose detail tickets are its sub-issues off the board: one builder, one branch, one verify, one merge, one deploy, while every sub-issue keeps its own checks, Annahmen, numbers and a `**Gemergt:**` line with the package's merge sha. Before opening a ticket, search the open ones for overlap and extend an existing one instead of creating a twin. The branch name contains the ticket id:
`feat/<id>-<short-slug>`, `fix/<id>-…`, `ci/<id>-…`, `docs/<id>-…`. Branch from the current `main`, unless the ticket or its epic
names an umbrella branch ( stacked work{{UMBRELLA_NOTE}} ): then branch from that and merge back into it. An umbrella branch and `main` are merged into each other once per batch of tickets, with the verify command run on the merged tree each time.

- Commit work in progress early and often on the branch ( at least every 30 minutes, or post a one-line progress note ): a restarted session must not lose it, and a stalled agent shows by its missing commits.
- A new worktree needs its dependencies installed ( `{{LOCAL_RUN}}` or the repo's install step ) before any check runs in it; a check that fails for a missing module proves nothing.
- Squash only onto the branch's own base ( `git reset --soft $( git merge-base HEAD origin/main )` ), never onto an
  `origin/main` that a fetch has moved: the squashed tree would silently undo what was merged meanwhile.
- Bring `main` in by merging it into the branch, never by rebasing a pushed branch. No force-push.
- Merge, verify and push run under the plugin's merge lock ( `scripts/mergelock.sh` ), one builder at a time per repository, so nobody verifies twice because the branch moved.
- **Merge, test, push in one chain with `&&`**, never with `;`: `git merge … && <verify> && git push …`. A push must never go out before the test result is read.
- **The orchestrator decides the deploy, once per batch, never a builder; a deployer agent does the work.** After the merges of a batch the orchestrator triggers one small **deployer agent** ( the cheapest model ), never two at once. Under the merge lock ( `scripts/mergelock.sh`, so no merge lands meanwhile ) it runs `{{VERIFY}}` on the integration branch's tip ( `main` or the umbrella ), which must pass on exactly that tip, builds, and deploys that tip through the repository's single deploy script, which carries its own gates ( generated data present, the served page read back and naming this build's entry file, any other read-back the repo defines ). It returns one line ( sha, entry file, read-back result ); the orchestrator only decides when to deploy and writes that line into `STATE.md` ( Last hand-backs ) and, where the repo wants it, as a line on the package card. A builder's prompt has no deploy step; a builder that needs a deployed state to test says so in its hand-over. A deploy is finished when the served page has been read back and names this build's entry file, not when the upload returns. Deploy scripts upload the entry page every time.
- A deploy ships the built site and static assets, nothing else: **never an executable server-side file** ( PHP, CGI, shell scripts, handlers in `.htaccess` ), not even briefly, and no server configuration or new credentials. Free space and quotas come from the server's own FTP commands, from {{OWNER_NAME}}'s control panel, or are reported as unknown so {{OWNER_NAME}} decides.
- A build must leave the working tree clean. A file a build regenerates is either ignored or committed, never left dirty at merge time.
- Generated data of any size ( tiles, caches, renders, datasets ) stays out of git: ignore it and write where it lives and how it is rebuilt into the ticket. Hosting it is {{OWNER_NAME}}'s decision.
- Branches werden aufgeräumt, sobald die Karte in Fertig ist ( bis dahin kann {{OWNER_NAME}} noch Änderungen verlangen ): Remote-Branch löschen ( `git push origin --delete <branch>` ), lokale Worktrees entfernen ( `git worktree remove` ).
- Several agents run at once: each starts its dev servers on its own ports ( a fixed default port per app, or `--port <n>` ) and stops only the processes it started, by their PID. {{OWNER_NAME}}'s own dev server port is never touched.
- Headless browser checks never touch {{OWNER_NAME}}'s machine: they run muted and windowless ( `headless: 'new'`, `--mute-audio`, no `bringToFront` or target activation, no window position or focus calls, no OS input tools ), through one central launcher per repository, under the plugin's watchdog `scripts/run.sh <timeout s> <command>`, which ends the command after a timeout and kills orphaned Chromes. The app under test gets a flag that creates no audio context at all ( the repository names it ), because even a muted headless browser that opens one makes the operating system reconfigure the shared output device and {{OWNER_NAME}} hears pops. Headless browsers share the GPU with {{OWNER_NAME}}'s browser: at most the `headless` that `scripts/capacity.sh` recommends right now ( measured; upper bound `headlessMax`, `.factory.json`, default 4 ) run at once on the machine, and none starts while the 1-minute load average is above the core count ( `run.sh` waits for both ). When none is free, browser work waits; building goes on. {{OWNER_NAME}}'s own dev server and browser are never touched. Headless checks never run {{OWNER_NAME}}'s installed browser bundle ( on macOS the app bundle under /Applications ): the operating system then treats every headless instance as 'the browser is running', so {{OWNER_NAME}}'s own browser will not start, and focus, keyboard and the audio session are routed to the wrong process. Use a separate browser build ( Chrome for Testing, installed into a cache folder by a repo script ) through the repo's single launcher, with an env override for the path. The same holds for **every other headless process that could open an audio device**: Blender runs with `-noaudio`, ffmpeg never plays back, Python / Node audio libraries stay off; opening a device makes CoreAudio reconfigure the shared output and pops into whatever {{OWNER_NAME}} is playing, even when the process is silent.
- Merging into a worktree another agent is working in changes files under it: say so in the ticket, and prefer merging when that agent
  is between steps.
- When you name a ticket to {{OWNER_NAME}}, name its title too: "#31 ( Title )", never a bare number.
